title: Routine cards, review gates and a log that proves it works

say: Routine cards, review gates and a log that proves it works.
This is the video for module two of AI Productivity Systems.
A system that produces fast drafts but lets errors through is worse than no system, because people stop trusting your work.

say: In this video you will choose your tools, turn tasks into routine cards, and add the checks and the log that keep the system honest.

items: Choose a lean, low-data tool stack

say: Every extra app is another password and more data used. So pick one tool for each job: one place to capture, and one assistant.

panel.heading: One tool for each of four jobs
items: Capture: notes app or a chat with yourself
Assistant: one AI tool with your context
Home for files: one Drive or one folder
Calendar and reminders to fire routines

say: One home for files, and a calendar to fire each routine. Stay with your choice for at least a month before judging it.
To save data, prefer typed chats, upload big files on Wi-Fi, and make your documents available offline.

panel.heading: One tool for each of four jobs
items: Capture: notes app or a chat with yourself
Assistant: one AI tool with your context
Home for files: one Drive or one folder
Calendar and reminders to fire routines

say: Complete all five before you load your context store into any tool.
Fraudsters sell fake AI apps and cheap shared logins on WhatsApp. Install apps only from the official store, pay only inside the official app or website, and never share your login or one-time codes.

panel.heading: Account safety setup
items: Unique strong password
Two-step verification switched on
Chat data settings reviewed
Phone screen lock enabled
Offline master copy saved

say: A good intention fades within weeks. A routine card does not, because it answers every question in advance. When you are tired, you follow the card.

panel.heading: A one-page recipe for one task
items: Trigger: a fixed time or event
Inputs: exactly what you gather first
Saved prompt: your tested wording
Check: what you verify before sending
Output and time box, then log the run

say: It says when the routine happens, what you gather, and which saved prompt you run.

panel.heading: A one-page recipe for one task
items: Trigger: a fixed time or event
Inputs: exactly what you gather first
Saved prompt: your tested wording
Check: what you verify before sending
Output and time box, then log the run

say: Then what you check, where the result goes, and how many minutes you allow. The AI works only in the middle. You own the inputs, the check and the delivery.

panel.heading: A one-page recipe for one task
items: Trigger: a fixed time or event
Inputs: exactly what you gather first
Saved prompt: your tested wording
Check: what you verify before sending
Output and time box, then log the run

say: Assistants sometimes round or recalculate numbers. So let a spreadsheet do the sums, tell the AI not to change any figure, and still check every figure yourself.

Output and time box, then log the run
panel.rule: Prompts with numbers say: Do not calculate or change any figure.

say: The sheet shows 135,000 naira collected and 15,000 naira outstanding. Only these totals go into her saved prompt, with the words: do not name anyone who owes.

say: She checks every figure against her sheet, and changes most members to 26 of 30 members. Then she writes private reminders herself, so nobody is shamed in the group.
Member names, phone numbers and amounts per person never enter the AI tool. The routine now takes about 20 minutes.

panel.heading: Match the check to the risk

cards.d: Your own notes or a first list of ideas. A quick read for sense.
Messages to members or clients, reports, posts. The full five-point check.
Money, health, legal or official matters. Every claim sourced, plus a second reviewer.

say: Messages to members, reports and posts get the full five-point check: names and dates, numbers, private data, sources, and does it sound like you. Watch for invented details, like a venue you never supplied.

say: Log one line for every run: date, routine, minutes, edit level and errors caught. Ngozi logged 12 runs over four weeks. They took 240 minutes, against 520 without AI. She saved 280 minutes.

panel.heading: Ngozi reads four weeks of her log
items: 520 minutes without AI, 240 with it
Saved: 280 minutes in four weeks
Heavy edits: 3 of 12 runs
Errors caught at the gate: 5

say: Only 3 runs needed heavy edits, and her gate caught 5 errors, including two wrong dates. They came from an old facts sheet, so she fixed the facts sheet, not the prompt.

panel.heading: Ngozi reads four weeks of her log
items: 520 minutes without AI, 240 with it

Errors caught at the gate: 5

say: If a routine saves time but needs heavy edits often, fix it. If it still saves under 10 minutes after fixing, drop it. Doing a task by hand is a valid result.

panel.rule: Keep it if it saves 10+ minutes a run, heavy edits at most 1 in 3.

say: To remember. Keep your stack lean and secure. Write routine cards. Let the spreadsheet do the sums. Set your check by risk. And let your own log decide which routines stay. Every card also needs a fallback for days with no AI or no data.

panel.heading: Remember
items: One tool per job, set up safely
Routine cards: trigger, inputs, prompt, check, output
Sums come from the sheet, never the AI
Set the review gate by risk
Your own log decides keep, fix or drop
